events.headline: Jake Ferguson has a low ankle sprain after leaving Sunday on the first drive
events.detail: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports a low ankle sprain, with no timetable given. Ferguson exited on Dallas' first possession against Arizona without a catch. With Luke Schoonmaker (groin) inactive, Brevyn Spann-Ford played most of the remaining snaps and James Mitchell was elevated. Dallas plays at Indianapolis in Week 9.
events.so_what: A low sprain is the better version of this injury, but treat him as week-to-week until he practices. Have a Week 9 tight end ready; Spann-Ford inherits snaps, not a proven target share, so he is a last resort rather than a bid.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Cowboys hit with troubling Jake Ferguson injury update (Nov. 2)

events.headline: Lamar Jackson (right thumb) to have surgery and go on IR; Tyler Huntley also hurt
events.detail: Jackson injured his right thumb on his first pass back from a high ankle sprain and will have surgery and go on injured reserve; coach Jesse Minter said it could be season-ending, per The Baltimore Sun's Brian Wacker via RotoWire. Tyler Huntley left in the first quarter with a toe injury and is expected to have an MRI this week, per ESPN. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the 36-10 loss and could make his first start Thursday against Jacksonville; Baltimore is expected to add quarterback depth first. Zay Flowers finished with no catches on five targets, and Derrick Henry has been under 60 rushing yards for three straight games.
events.so_what: Jackson is an IR stash at best and a drop if the season-ending read holds. Nobody at this quarterback spot is worth starting until Baltimore names one, and the downgrade hits Flowers and Mark Andrews on TD odds. Henry faces more stacked boxes on a short week, so lower him as well.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love hurts his right ankle in his first game back; Tyler Allgeier scores twice with Bam Knight also out
events.detail: Love left in the first quarter and did not return, after missing two games with a left ankle sprain; ESPN calls it his third ankle injury of the year, and the team has not announced a diagnosis. Knight left with a concussion in the second quarter. Allgeier played all 40 second-half and overtime snaps per PFF, with 11 carries for 147 yards and five catches for 44 yards, and a touchdown each way. Arizona plays at Seattle on Nov. 8.
events.so_what: Love is a hold with no timeline until imaging lands, and a repeat ankle makes a multi-week absence realistic. Allgeier is the start here if Love sits: the snap share is the real signal and the 147 yards came largely on two long runs, so expect volume RB2 rather than a repeat.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty gets two carries as Mike Washington Jr. takes 25; Kubiak says it was 'my call'
events.detail: In the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets, Mike Washington Jr. started, carried 25 times for 83 yards (3.3 per carry, stuffed six times per ESPN), took early-down and goal-line work, and played 63% of the snaps to Jeanty's 37%. Jeanty ran twice for 9 yards and caught three passes for 64 yards as the receiving back. Klint Kubiak said, "That's my call, and Ashton is still going to be a big part of our team," and that Jeanty's pregame comments about the Jets were not a factor. Jeanty said he was told during the week that Washington would get more work. No starter has been named for Week 9 at San Francisco.
events.so_what: A planned role change matters more than Washington's inefficient 3.3 a carry. Washington has early-down and goal-line work, which is where TD points live, so he is a live FLEX. Jeanty is a matchup start on receiving yards until Kubiak shows the carries are coming back. ESPN expects a rebound; the Kubiak quote does not promise one.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Klint Kubiak explains Ashton Jeanty's decreased role vs. Jets (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Colts bench Daniel Jones in a 42-7 loss; Steichen will "evaluate everything," with Anthony Richardson next up
events.detail: Jones was pulled with 11:53 left after going 19-of-28 for 144 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions at Jacksonville. Anthony Richardson finished and completed both passes for 8 yards. Asked about Jones, Shane Steichen said, "I'm going to evaluate everything, every position going forward," the first time he has not reaffirmed him. Dallas visits in Week 9.
events.so_what: No starter has been named. A Richardson start is what would change value here: his rushing scores at RB rates under the konami premium, so even an inaccurate game has a floor. Claim him only as a speculative stash until Steichen says it. A QB change also makes every Colts receiver a wider-range start.

source.label: ESPN: Colts' Shane Steichen to 'evaluate everything,' including QB (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Gardner Minshew replaces Jacoby Brissett and leads an overtime win; ESPN expects him to start at Seattle
events.detail: Mike LaFleur benched Brissett (10 of 23, 119 yards, an interception) late in the third quarter, down 17-3. Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns in a 33-30 overtime win at Dallas. ESPN's Josh Weinfuss reports Minshew is expected to stay the starter, though LaFleur would not confirm it. Michael Wilson caught 8 of a team-high 15 targets for 111 yards while playing with broken ribs.
events.so_what: Not a streamer yet: Seattle is next and a pocket quarterback at 4 points a pass TD has little floor. The useful part is Wilson, whose target count made him the receiver to start in this offense, provided the ribs hold up through the week.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: LaFleur noncommittal, but Cardinals reportedly expected to keep starting Minshew (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Jonathan Taylor trade talks stay live after his fewest carries since 2023; Josh Downs has already asked out
events.detail: ESPN and NFL Network reported Indianapolis is willing to move Taylor and has talked with the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants and Seahawks; Taylor has not requested a trade. He played Sunday and had eight carries in the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, his fewest since October 2023. Steichen blamed the score ("It wasn't like we had a number on his carries"), and Taylor called his game "nowhere near up to par." Josh Downs asked to be traded earlier in the week and played 89.6% of the snaps before garbage time per PFF. The reports conflict on heat: CBS' Aditi Kinkhabwala was assured the Colts are not soliciting offers. The deadline is Nov. 10.
events.so_what: One blowout does not change Taylor's value; a landing spot could. He stays a start while a Colt, with Dallas next, but a trade into a shared backfield costs touches and a move would make Seth McGowan the speculative stash. Downs is a hold pending a destination.

source.label: ESPN: Colts' Shane Steichen to 'evaluate everything,' including QB (Nov. 1)

events.headline: DJ Moore (knee) hurt late in his return, says it is not serious; Joshua Palmer (hamstring) ruled out
events.detail: Moore had his best game since Week 1 in the win over Baltimore, then hurt his knee late; he says it is not serious and his status will be monitored, per ESPN. Palmer left with a hamstring injury and was ruled out, per PFF. Dalton Kincaid (chest), also active after a Questionable tag, caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo faces Minnesota in Week 9.
events.so_what: Moore's own word is not a clearance, so wait for the Wednesday practice report before counting on him. If he or Palmer misses time, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir get the snaps. Kincaid stays locked in at a scarce position.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) leaves at Miami and does not return; Eli Raridon plays 92% of snaps
events.detail: Henry was ruled out for the rest of the game with a foot injury. Rookie Eli Raridon played 92% of the offensive snaps per PFF, with one catch for five yards. New England also played without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, and got long touchdowns from Kyle Williams (43 yards) and DeMario Douglas (48 yards) in the 24-19 win.
events.so_what: Henry is uncertain for Week 9 against Green Bay until the practice report. Raridon's snap count is real but one catch says he is not yet a target, so he is a speculative add only if you are already out of tight ends.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) sits again as Braelon Allen runs for a career-high 147; Hall could return next week
events.detail: Hall was inactive against Las Vegas, his fifth straight missed game. Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards, his third 100-yard game since taking over, per ESPN. Hall could return next week, and trade speculation around him is growing ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
events.so_what: Allen is a start while Hall sits, but his value depends on the Week 9 practice report and any trade. If Hall returns the job is a real question, not an automatic handback. Hall stays on benches until he gets past limited practice.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 big takeaways and fantasy spin from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Jonah Coleman takes over the Broncos backfield with RJ Harvey on IR and J.K. Dobbins fading
events.detail: Coleman led the backfield for a second straight week with a 68% snap rate, 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, and four catches for 63 yards. He ran 16 routes, played 19 of 21 second-half snaps per PFF, and scored the go-ahead touchdown against Kansas City. Dobbins averaged 1.9 yards per carry. Harvey went on IR Saturday with a knee injury and is eligible no earlier than Week 13.
events.so_what: This is a lead-back role with routes attached, and Harvey's absence removes a competitor for at least four more games. Coleman is a weekly RB2/FLEX start and the top priority if still on your wire. Dobbins is a bench hold on goal-line hopes only.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combine for 310 rushing yards as Tampa Bay splits the work
events.detail: Irving ran 27 times for 170 yards and a touchdown and led early downs. Gainwell rushed for 140 yards and took all the passing-down snaps per PFF. Gainwell has 14-plus carries in back-to-back games. Sean Tucker was active but played no offensive snaps. Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 in a game ESPN says was limited by weather.
events.so_what: Irving stays a start with a TD role, though a real split lowers his ceiling. Gainwell has moved past handcuff status: a FLEX option on volume alone and the priority insurance add behind Irving. A 50-plus carry day will not repeat, so price the role rather than the yardage.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams step up for Washington with Terry McLaurin out for the season
events.detail: McLaurin is on season-ending IR with a knee injury. Burks has taken the X spot and caught three passes for 81 yards, including a 53-yarder, in the 27-10 win over Philadelphia. Rookie slot man Williams caught a season-high 5 of 7 targets for 54 yards. Stefon Diggs, cleared after a full Thursday and Friday, played in 11 personnel. Running back Jeremy McNichols left in the third quarter with a foot injury, and Rachaad White led the team in carries.
events.so_what: Diggs is still the Commanders receiver to start. Williams has the steadier target path and Burks the big-play role, so both are bench adds rather than starts until a second game confirms it. McNichols' foot is worth watching for White's workload.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 big takeaways and fantasy spin from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley on a pitch count with hamstring and back, says his body is not where it needs to be
events.detail: Barkley played against Washington but ran 13 times for 30 yards and a Wildcat touchdown, and caught a 24-yard wheel route, in a 27-10 loss. Elijah Mitchell got 11 carries for 34 yards. Barkley said afterward, "my body's not really where I need [it] to be right now." Philadelphia has lost six straight and is starting Tanner McKee.
events.so_what: Played is not the same as healthy. The touchdown saved the day, and a split with Mitchell behind this offense makes Barkley a risky RB2 until he practices fully. Mitchell is a handcuff worth holding, with no value of his own on these numbers.

source.label: Philadelphia Inquirer: Eagles' offense stifled again in 27-10 loss to Commanders (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Tony Pollard posts a second straight 100-yard game with Tyjae Spears out; Titans now on bye
events.detail: Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns in the 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, playing 75%-plus of snaps with a 75%-plus rushing share in both games Spears (knee) has missed. Chimere Dike replaced Carnell Tate (shoulder) and caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown; Michael Carter took the receiving-back role. Cam Ward threw for 304 yards. Tennessee has a Week 9 bye.
events.so_what: Pollard is a real RB2 while Spears is out, but the bye means he helps no one this week. Plan the bye now: don't drop him, and fill the slot before Tuesday. Dike is a stash until Tate's status is known.

source.label: ESPN: Week 8 fantasy winners and losers (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Adonai Mitchell breaks out for 142 yards against Las Vegas as Omar Cooper Jr. goes catchless
events.detail: Mitchell, acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade, caught seven passes for 142 yards and a touchdown and played 95% of the Jets' 11 personnel snaps, but only 23% in 12 personnel, per PFF. Cooper finished with no catches. Garrett Wilson remains a favored target.
events.so_what: The snap share is worth a bench spot, the yardage is not repeatable on its own. His low 12-personnel rate means he comes off the field in some looks, so wait for a second game before starting him over a settled FLEX.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Mike Gesicki plays a season-high 67.6% of snaps and scores again with Cincinnati tight ends thinned out
events.detail: Gesicki caught four passes for 76 yards and a touchdown against Tennessee, including 90% of third-down snaps, per PFF. Cam Grandy played three snaps and Jack Endries 12 in a 74-snap game, with Tanner Hudson and Erick All on IR. SI has Gesicki scoring in five straight games. Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards.
events.so_what: Rising snaps in a high-volume offense make this a real tight end start, not just a TD streak. In a position with so few startable options, he is worth starting over a streamer while the snaps hold.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet cleared for his 2026 debut Monday vs. Chicago; Jadarian Price still needs a roster move
events.detail: Charbonnet has been activated from PUP and is cleared to play. Price is off the injury report but remains on injured reserve; Mike Macdonald would only say, "We have a plan for Zach and with JD," and that any move "would happen on Monday," adding, "We're going to let the transaction speak for itself." Seattle does not have to restore Price for at least two more weeks. No snap split has been announced, and Emanuel Wilson's lead role likely shrinks.
events.so_what: Three backs and no announced split on a Monday night is the worst case for a lineup: bench all of them unless you have nothing else, and read the snap shares before setting Week 9 against Arizona.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Mike Macdonald hasn't committed to Jadarian Price playing on Monday (Nov. 1)

events.headline: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson sat at Miami; Rhamondre Stevenson played 77% of snaps
events.detail: Both were downgraded to out on Saturday, Brown (ankle, knee) after sitting out Thursday and Friday and Henderson with an illness. Stevenson played 77% of the offensive snaps per PFF, with Corey Kiner the primary backup. Efton Chism III led the team with five catches, and DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams each scored from long range. Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are on IR.
events.so_what: Week 9 against Green Bay turns on the Wednesday report for both. Henderson's illness should clear quicker than Brown's knee, which has been flaring. Stevenson is a FLEX if Henderson sits again; Douglas is a one-week add at most.

source.label: PFF: Week 8 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways from Sunday's games (Nov. 1)

events.headline: NFL to review new abuse allegations against Josh Jacobs as its open investigation continues
events.detail: The league said Saturday it will review allegations disclosed in a public records release Friday night "as part of the investigation which has remained open," per ESPN. Jacobs' attorneys called them uncorroborated and old. He pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges in September. No status change has been reported and no timeline has been given. Jacobs played 71% of the snaps in the Thursday win over Carolina, per Packers On SI; Lloyd played 11 snaps.
events.so_what: He remains eligible for now, so lineups don't change today. Any discipline would land with little warning, and MarShawn Lloyd is the back to look at as insurance if you roster Jacobs.

source.label: ESPN: NFL to review additional allegations against Packers RB Josh Jacobs (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Colston Loveland cleared, no designation for Monday night at Seattle after a full Saturday practice
events.detail: Loveland (neck) was limited Friday and a full participant Saturday, and Chicago gave him no game designation, per NFL.com. Kyle Monangai (toe) remains out.
events.so_what: He plays. Starting tight ends are scarce in every one of these formats, so a cleared every-week TE goes straight back into the lineup; the Monday slot also means you can still pivot if anything changes over the weekend.

source.label: NFL.com: news roundup, Saturday Oct. 31

events.headline: Kyle Monangai (turf toe) ruled out for Monday night at Seattle
events.detail: Ben Johnson told reporters Monangai has been ruled out for Week 8, per The Big Lead. He has not practiced since the turf toe and has missed every game since Week 4.
events.so_what: Out is out: he comes out of any Monday slot now, before Sunday locks, so fill it with a Sunday player.

source.label: The Big Lead: Breece Hall, Kyle Monangai and more RB injury updates for Week 8 (Oct. 31)

events.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) ruled out for Monday night vs. Chicago
events.detail: Shaheed was ruled out after missing Thursday and Friday practice, per FOX 13's Curtis Crabtree via RotoWire. It is his first missed game of 2026; the knee was hurt in the Week 7 win over Kansas City. Tory Horton and Cooper Kupp are expected to absorb more snaps behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and his next chance is Week 9 vs. Arizona.
events.so_what: Swap him out now with a Sunday player rather than waiting on Monday. Horton gains snaps but is a dart throw, not a start.

source.label: RotoWire: Rashid Shaheed ruled out for MNF (Oct. 31)

events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out for Sunday night at Washington
events.detail: Smith missed practice all week and is listed as out, per RotoWire; Wicks is also out, so both sit for a second straight game. RotoWire expects Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to handle most of the receiver snaps, with Tanner McKee at quarterback after Jalen Hurts went to IR.
events.so_what: Bench both. The targets spread across four receivers behind a backup quarterback, so none of them is a confident start; Lemon is the name to watch if the snaps concentrate, but not a bid on one game of a rotation.

source.label: RotoWire: DeVonta Smith ruled out for Sunday's game (Oct. 30)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) ruled out vs. Atlanta; concussion no longer the issue
events.detail: Egbuka has been ruled out for Sunday against the Falcons with a foot injury, per Scott Smith of the Bucs' official site via RotoWire. His next chance to play is Week 9 against Chicago, and Tampa Bay has its bye the following week. RotoWire expects Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst to take more snaps alongside slot man Chris Godwin.
events.so_what: Out this week, and a Week 9 return then a bye means one game in the next two at best if the foot lingers. Godwin is the Bucs receiver to start; Johnson and Hurst split the rest and neither is worth a bid on a one-week opening.

source.label: RotoWire: Emeka Egbuka ruled out for Week 8 (Oct. 30)
